# dsh-tasks-panel
中文 · English
A to-do list, a calendar of what actually happened, and a push at the exact minute — inside DeepSeek
ist, a calendar of what actually happened, and a push at the exact minute — inside DeepSeek Harness.

Most task lists ask you to live in them. This one lives where you already work: it is a sidebar
pane

l of the DeepSeek Harness app, so the agent can add and close tasks through a tool, and you can
chec

k or edit them without leaving the session you were in — plus a Back button that puts you right
back

ithout leaving the session you were in — plus a Back button that puts you right
back where you were.
## What it does
| 🗂 **Sidebar entry** | One more icon in the rail. Click it for the panel, or use **Back** to return

to the session, Plugins, Schedules — whatever you left. |
| ✅ **To do** | Add, complete, reopen, de
lete. The date defaults to today, the clock to the next five-minute mark, and `×` clears the date fo

r undated notes. |
| 👀 **Today at a glance** | Hover the sidebar icon: a floating agenda lists today
's tasks with their times, anything overdue, and how much is still open. No click, no context switch

. |
| 🗓 **Calendar** | Every event — added, finished, reopened, edited, deleted — is drawn on the mo

nth grid. Click a day to read its log. |
| 💬 **Hover preview** | Point at a task or a day for the fu
ll card: title, note, due date and time, source, session, timestamps. Cards dodge the sidebar instea

d of covering it. |
| ⏰ **Feishu reminders** | Paste a group-bot webhook once. At the due minute the
host pushes `⏰ title / time / note` to your phone — and closes the task, so an appointment you kept

does not sit in the list waiting for a click. |
| 🤖 **Agent tool** | `task_write` lets the assistan
t add and close tasks — same operations as the UI, so the two never diverge. |

## Reminders

Reminders follow one rule: **a task is reminded only when it has both a date and a time.** A date
al
one is a to-do for the day, not an appointment, so it stays quiet.
| Rule | Why |

| The host scans every 30 seconds | DSH must be running; a closed app cannot push. |
| One push per

`date` + `time` slot | `notifiedFor` remembers, so a re-start does not re-notify. |
| Moving a task

to a new time re-arms it | An appointment that moved deserves a new reminder. |
| A slot more than 6
hours old is marked, not pushed | A laptop asleep overnight should not dump yesterday on you at 9 a

.m. |
| The switch saves by itself, webhook included | Pressing the switch then forgetting Save is h

ow "enabled: false" happens. |
| A delivered reminder closes the task | An appointment that has happ
ened is done; coming back to tick it is busywork. Turn **Close the task once it is pushed** off to k

eep tasks open. |
| Only a real push closes it | Tasks skipped by the six-hour window stay open — si

lence is not completion. |
| `task_write` has no reminder action | Turning on a push to your phone i
s your decision, not the agent's. |
The panel shows the last send time and the last delivery error, and **Send a test** proves the phone
receives it before you trust it with anything real. Signature-checked Feishu bots are supported by
pasting the secret too.
## Data

Everything lives in the `dsh_tasks` storage domain: `tasks` and `events` tables plus a `global`
reco

rd for reminder settings. The browser half talks to the host over
`POST /api/dsh-tasks-panel/op`. No
thing leaves the machine except the Feishu push itself.

`zod@3.25.76` is vendored under `node_modules/zod` because a bundle installed by link
(`"dsh-tasks-p

anel": "link:…"`) does not get its dependencies installed by pnpm. An npm install pulls
zod from the
registry instead, so the published tarball deliberately does not ship `node_modules`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| suite | what it covers |
| `node test/host.mjs` (38 checks) | storage ops (`add`/`complete`/`reopen`/`update`/`remove`/`clear

Completed`), time normalisation, the HTTP-op surface, the `task_write` tool |
| `node test/reminders
.mjs` (34 checks) | Feishu scheduling: due detection, one push per slot, the six-hour grace window,
auto-completion on delivery, the one-shot sweep of tasks reminded before 0.5.2, signature signing, e

rror reporting, the settings guard |
| `node test/ui.mjs` (73 checks) | the client half rendered in
jsdom: slot registration, to-do rows, all three hover cards, the compose form's defaults, the first-
run guide, the settings card with both switches |
Everything runs against the real bundle — no mocks of our own code. The host suites import `index.js

`
with a fake Cordis context and in-memory tables; the UI suite loads `client.js` through a stand-in

`window.__ModuleLoader__` and renders the panel into jsdom. No network: Feishu calls go to a stub
`
fetch` that records the payload it would have sent.
GitHub Actions runs the same suites on Node 20 and 22 for every push and pull request, and publishes
to npm from a tag through OIDC trusted publishing (`.github/workflows/`).
